_comment: Sync manifest — the single home for what a sync delivers: the starter files, the tool configs, the skills corpus and destination, the guard files a project must wire, and the project-local paths to ignore. Read by BOTH entry points — sync-manager.ps1 (GUI) and sync-guidelines.ps1 (CLI) — which must produce identical project outputs. WHICH skills fit a given project is NOT decided here: plan-skills.js owns that, and this file only names the corpus and the destination.

mirror._comment: The mirror is a WHOLE-TREE copy of `guidelines/` into a project's `_guidelines/` — robocopy /MIR, excluding `.git` and `.github` — and check-sync-drift.js hashes the whole tree on both sides. This section used to declare `include` and `exclude` lists that NO script ever read, and the live mirrors contradicted `include` outright: they carry global-configs/fragments, global-configs/scripts and sync-manifest.json, none of which the list named. Half of `exclude` named repo-root paths (`docs`, `sync-manager.ps1`, `sync-projects.json`, `node_modules`) that are not inside the copy source at all, so it could never have applied. Configuration that asserts authority nothing honours is worse than none — it reads as a policy while being a comment. The two exclusions that ARE honoured live in the robocopy call in GuidelineSync.psm1, which is the one implementation both entry points now share.

backups._comment: Created by `sync-guidelines.ps1 -Backup` (New-DatedBackupDir). Declared unconditionally rather than only on a -Backup run: an ignore line for a directory that does not exist yet costs nothing, and a conditional entry is the one forgotten on the run that needs it. Before this section existed the entry lived nowhere, so a -Backup sync left an untracked directory — and the `clean-tree` step of the pre-push gate fails on an untracked directory.

guards._comment: The guard scripts a project must EXPOSE as an npm script. The mirror delivers the files, but a file nobody runs is a control that exists only in a directory listing — so this is the one home for 'which controls a project must have'. Declared rather than derived from the guards' own `@tier`, because a tier says WHEN a guard runs, not WHERE it is meaningful: `check-links.js` guards the guidelines tree and is meaningless in a project, while `check-doc-census.js` enforces one home per fact in every project. `check-sync-drift.js` verifies each project's package.json runs every file named here, by file and not by script name — the doctrine maps each step to the project's own names.

starters.description: Project constitution — primary AI agent rules, all inline. Created once; never overwritten on re-sync (user owns this file).
Project overview — the single home for what-this-is, structure, and quick start. Replaces the deleted AI_CONTEXT.md / ARCHITECTURE_INDEX.md.
Detailed technical reference for all subsystems — loaded on demand
GitHub Copilot pointer file — redirects to AGENTS.md (single source of rules). Created once; never overwritten on re-sync.

skills._comment: `_skills/` is a FILTERED mirror, not a whole-directory copy: only the skills that fit a project's stack are delivered, and the decision lives in one place — global-configs/scripts/lib/plan-skills.js. So `check-sync-drift.js` verifies each project against the PLAN that selector produces (every planned skill present and byte-identical, nothing left behind), never against this whole source corpus. A whole-corpus hash comparison would report every project as drifted by construction, because a filtered subset is the correct delivery.
skills.agentsMdSectionBody: Skill files live at `_skills/<name>/SKILL.md` — the Agent Skills standard layout. Only the skills that fit THIS project's stack are copied; load one when its trigger matches the current task.
skills.deliveryDecision: WHY `_skills/` STAYS GITIGNORED — recorded 2026-10-19, and it was a choice, not an oversight. `AGENTS.md` is committed and links to `_skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, which is not; so in a fresh clone every link in the inventory 404s, and an agent told the project carries twelve skills finds none of them. The two honest resolutions are `commit the skills` and `stop advertising them as if they were there`. Committing was NOT taken, for two reasons about this fleet rather than about taste: (1) the delivery model is explicit — the `_guidelines/` mirror is gitignored too, so the steering corpus is local by design and the sync is the mechanism that brings it in; a project repo carries its own constitution, not a copy of the central corpus. (2) All seven registered projects run a `clean-tree` pre-push step that fails on ANY dirty or untracked file, so tracking `_skills/` would turn every upstream skill edit into a blocked push across seven repositories until each change was committed and reviewed. The branch taken instead makes the inventory honest about the mirror's lifecycle — the block says `_skills/` is a synced mirror, present after a sync and absent in a fresh clone until one runs, and names the canonical source it was copied from — and lets `check-sync-drift.js` fail a project that has no `_skills/` at all. Reversing this is a one-line change here plus a `git add` in each project; it is a recorded owner decision because it changes what a project repository contains.

registry._comment: sync-projects.json is the registry of target projects: WHERE the fleet is, and WHAT was delivered to it WHEN. It is not a statement about the present. The field that read `"status": "synced"` recorded how the last sync attempt ended and was named as though it meant the current state; measured 2026-10-19 the registry read `synced` for all seven projects while `npm run sync:drift` was failing seven of seven. A registry whose fields read like current-state claims WILL be believed, so the field was renamed to say what it actually holds. The current state is the verdict `npm run sync:drift` prints. The recorded hashes say what content was delivered, and when — and nothing but the sync itself may write a hash, because that is what makes the record mean `this content was delivered`.

fields.path: absolute path to the project directory
fields.name: display name
fields.lastSyncOutcome: synced | failed — the OUTCOME OF THE LAST SYNC ATTEMPT, not the current state
fields.lastSynced: when the last successful sync ran
fields.contentHash: hash of the guidelines source at that moment — written only by the sync, never by a check
fields.skillsHash: hash of the skills corpus at that moment

vscodeCopilotInstructions.comment: Always prefer the project-local AGENTS.md — it is self-contained and always present after sync.
